I want to get this: http://www.ebay.ca/itm/Dell-PowerVault-MD3000-AMP01-SAS-SATA-Hard-Disk-Array-1TB-Trays-2x-Ctrl-2x-PSU-/271921410796?pt=LH_DefaultDomain_2&hash=item3f4fc772ec[1]

And this http://www.ebay.ca/itm/DELL-0M778G-PERC5-Dual-RAID-SAS-PCI-e-Storage-Card-/201382798648?pt=LH_DefaultDomain_2&hash=item2ee359a538[2]

For storage. As you can see, it has space for 15 drives, way more than the 4 slots I have now.

This is the system I intend to put the SAS card in. I know it's not powerful, it just has to run FreeNAS. http://ca.pcpartpicker.com/p/QNCDsY[3]

Oh, and I might get a quad gigabit card if I need more speed.

Now, my existing server runs Plex. As you may know, Plex is very resource intensive, way too much for the box I'm building. So I plan on using a VM on my existing Proxmox server for Plex. FreeNAS will be hooked up to Proxmox.

Will this all work as I intend? I have no experience with SAS and direct attached storage, is there anything I need to know? Can FreeNAS make a RAID volume larger on the fly?

I do want to make it clear, I want every HDD to show up seperately in the OS. I don't plan on RAIDing them together. Will that work? And can I use 2 cables from the 2 SAS ports on the back of the card to the 2 IN ports on the powervault?
Can someone help me with my new storage upgrade? I don't know what I'm doing.

I believe to expand your RAID you are going to have to blow away the old and create a new. If this were my server I would use opensuse as my OS because compared to other Linux distros and FreeNAS, OpenSuse tends to focus the most heavily on storage and the needs of storage deployments. It's become the favoured solution for people doing storage whereas CentOS is favoured for people building app servers.

OpenSuse is more aggressive with their inclusion and support of filesystems. They have more of them and they have new ones sooner than other Linux distros. OpenSuse puts an effort into supporting DRBD and storage clustering which is often an afterthought or might not exist on other platforms.

When the day comes you plan on filling the drive bays, I would backup the data, create one big RAID 10 and install opensuse and away you go.
